et kærlighedsforhold.explanation: "Et kærlighedsforhold" means "a romantic relationship". It is built from "kærlighed" (love) and "et forhold" (a relationship). "Forhold" also names other kinds of relationships: "et godt forhold til min chef" (a good relationship with my boss).

et køkken.explanation: "Et køkken" means "a kitchen". When you talk about a style of cooking, it means "cuisine": "det danske køkken" (Danish cuisine).

et køkkenbord.explanation: "Et køkkenbord" means "a kitchen table / counter". It is built from "et køkken" (a kitchen) and "et bord" (a table). When you prepare food on it, it means "a kitchen counter": "Jeg skærer brød på køkkenbordet" (I cut bread on the kitchen counter).

et køkkenur.explanation: "Et køkkenur" means "a kitchen timer". It is built from "et køkken" (a kitchen) and "et ur" (a clock). The part "ur" also means "a watch": "Min far har et nyt ur" (My dad has a new watch).

et køleskab.explanation: "Et køleskab" means "a fridge". It is built from "at køle" (to cool) and "et skab" (a cupboard), so it is literally a "cooling cupboard". "Skab" also ends "et klædeskab" (a wardrobe).

et køn.explanation: "Et køn" means "a gender / sex". To include everyone, say "begge køn" (both genders): "Kurset er for begge køn" (The course is for both genders).

et kønummer.explanation: "Et kønummer" means "a queue number". It is built from "en kø" (a queue) and "et nummer" (a number). To get one from the machine, use "at trække" (to pull): "Jeg trækker et kønummer" (I take a queue number).

et kørekort.explanation: "Et kørekort" means "a driver's license". To say you earn one, use "at tage kørekort" (literally "to take a driver's license"): "Jeg tager kørekort i år" (I am getting my license this year).

et køretøj.explanation: "Et køretøj" means "a vehicle". It comes from "at køre" (to drive). The ending "tøj" also appears in "værktøj" (tools) and "legetøj" (toys).

kaffe.explanation: "Kaffe" means "a coffee". To order one, say "en kaffe, tak" (a coffee, please). To invite someone, ask "Skal vi have en kop kaffe?" (Shall we have a cup of coffee?).

kajak.explanation: "Kajak" means "kayaking". To say you go kayaking, use "at sejle i kajak" (to go by kayak): "Vi sejler i kajak på søen" (We go kayaking on the lake). When you mean the small boat, it means "a kayak": "en rød kajak" (a red kayak).

kakao.explanation: "Kakao" means "a cocoa". When you order the drink, it means "a hot chocolate": "En varm kakao, tak" (A hot chocolate, please).

kakaomælk.explanation: "Kakaomælk" means "chocolate milk". It is built from "kakao" (cocoa) and "mælk" (milk). For the hot drink, use "varm kakao" (hot cocoa): "En varm kakao, tak" (A hot cocoa, please).

kan du gentage det?.explanation: "Kan du gentage det?" means "Can you repeat that?". When you did not catch what someone said, ask this to hear it again. To ask more politely, add "tak" (please) at the end: "Kan du gentage det, tak?" (Can you repeat that, please?)

kan jeg betale med kort?.explanation: "Kan jeg betale med kort?" means "Can I pay by card?". It is built from "kan jeg" (can I), "betale" (pay), "med" (with) and "kort" (a card). To ask about a phone payment app, swap "kort" for "MobilePay": "Kan jeg betale med MobilePay?" (Can I pay with MobilePay?)

kan jeg købe ...?.explanation: "Kan jeg købe ...?" means "Can I buy ...?". "Kan jeg" means "can I". Say the item after "købe" (to buy): "Kan jeg købe en billet?" (Can I buy a ticket?) To ask politely in a shop or café, you can also say "Jeg vil gerne have en kaffe" (I would like a coffee).

kanel.explanation: "Kanel" means "cinnamon". The word is the first part of "en kanelsnegl" (a cinnamon roll), a pastry sold in Danish bakeries.

kaos.explanation: "Kaos" means "chaos". To say things are completely out of control, use "det rene kaos" (pure chaos): "Det er det rene kaos" (It is pure chaos). Spell it with a "k" and no "h".

karantæne.explanation: "En karantæne" means "a quarantine". To put people in quarantine, use "at sætte i karantæne": "Man sætter de syge i karantæne" (They put the sick people in quarantine). Spell it with a "k" and an "æ".

karry.explanation: "Karry" means "curry". The powder is called "karrypulver" (curry powder): "Jeg køber karrypulver" (I buy curry powder).

kartofler.explanation: "Kartofler" means "potatoes", the plural of "en kartoffel" (a potato). To say how potatoes are cooked, put a word in front: "kogte kartofler" (boiled potatoes).

kattemad.explanation: "Kattemad" means "cat food". It is built from "en kat" (a cat) and "mad" (food). The part "mad" also builds "morgenmad" (breakfast) and "aftensmad" (dinner).

ked af.explanation: "Ked af" means "sorry / sad". It is used after "er" (is): "Hun er ked af det" (She is sad). To say sorry after bumping into someone, use "undskyld" (sorry, excuse me) instead: "Undskyld, jeg ramte dig" (Sorry, I bumped into you).

ked af det.explanation: "Ked af det" means "sad". To say you are not sad, put "ikke" (not) before "ked": "Jeg er ikke ked af det" (I am not sad). When you say sorry for something you did, it also means "sorry": "Jeg er ked af, at jeg kom for sent" (I am sorry that I came late).

kedelig.explanation: "Kedelig" means "boring". When something is a pity, it means "unfortunate": "Det er kedeligt" (That is too bad). To say you yourself are bored, use "Jeg keder mig" (I am bored) instead.
